method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05; the dates in one module, the rules and exported questions in another, the cases in a third; three regulative rules (Schedule 2 cl 14 commence proceedings before the day; s 52A(1)(b) the respondent gives the complainant the statement within 14 days or the longer period allowed; ss 25(2)(b), 25A(4)(b) apply within 6 years) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. A layer beside baseline-2026-10 and naive-2026-10, which stay untouched. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Privacy Act 1988, Compilation No. 104, compilation date 4 June 2026 (includes amendments to Act No. 75, 2025; register id C2026C00227), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/C2004A03712.txt (retrieved 13 October 2026). Schedule 2 added by the Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024 (No. 128, 2024), commenced 10 June 2025 by endnote 3; that Act's application provision is not deposited. Not deposited: the State and Territory defamation Acts (the cl 11(5)(d) maximum is an input).

seat: the individual whose privacy was invaded: the plaintiff under the Schedule 2 statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy; the complainant or a class member of a representative complaint under Part V; the person who suffered loss from a credit reporting contravention under ss 25 and 25A

checks.l4: stable l4 of VS Code extension legalese.l4-vscode 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset
checks.command: l4 run pa-tort-dates.l4 ; l4 run pa-tort.l4 ; l4 run pa-tort-cases.l4
checks.result: 137 assertions written, 137 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text. One expectation changed in a scratch copy was reported as failing.

scope: Schedule 2 (statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy): cl 6(1) as the rules use it, cl 7(1), (2), (7), cls 8, 10, 11, 12 (with 9(1)), 13, 14, 15-18, 19, 20(1). Part V: ss 36(1)-(3), (5), 38, 38B(2), 39, 52(1)(b), (1AB), (1B), (3), (4), 52A(1)(b), 54(1), 55A(1), (5), (8), 62(1)-(3), (5), (6). Part IIIA Division 7: ss 25, 25A. Out: the APPs and Part IIIC (APPs 7, 12, 13 and Part IIIC are in baseline-2026-10; the other APPs are asked through 'may be an interference with privacy'); Schedule 2 Part 1, cls 7(3), (5), (6), 8A, 9(2), 11(6), 20(2), 21-23; the Commissioner's investigation, conciliation and procedure; civil penalties; the 2024 amending Act's application provision (not deposited). Reasons in NOTES.md.
focus: the provisions a claimant meets: the statutory tort (Schedule 2), representative complaints and determinations (Part V), compensation orders (ss 25, 25A)
